title: U.S. House · Montana's 2nd District
area: Eastern Montana, including Billings and Great Falls.

context.text: Incumbent Rep. Troy Downing (R) did not face a primary challenger in 2026, winning renomination unopposed.

summary.text: Troy Downing is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Montana's 2nd Congressional District. He is a former Montana state auditor and insurance commissioner who serves on the House Financial Services Committee and the Small Business Committee.

background.text: Raised in Indio, California; studied computer science at New York University.

Co-founded WebCal, an internet-based calendar system later incorporated into Yahoo in 1998, and was CEO of AC Self Storage Solutions; also operated a commercial real estate development firm and created a commercial insurance company.
Was previously a member of the Montana Land Board as a former statewide official.

priorities.text: Supports making the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act permanent and has introduced legislation aimed at expanding rural small businesses' access to capital.

Supports an "all-of-the-above" energy approach that emphasizes coal, oil and gas production in Montana, including legislation to keep the Bull Mountains coal mine open and to support Signal Peak's mining operations.

positions.summary: Supports making the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act's lower tax rates permanent and has cosponsored repeal of the federal estate tax.
Says fossil fuels are an abundant, cost-efficient energy source and supports coal, oil and gas production over restrictions aimed at reducing emissions.
Supports reducing federal involvement in education and says parents are best suited to make educational choices for their children.

record.text: Sits on the House Financial Services Committee and the Small Business Committee (Innovation, Entrepreneurship, and Workforce Development; and Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.
Introduced the Federal Insurance Office Elimination Act to eliminate the Federal Insurance Office.

Introduced the Expanding Access to Capital for Rural Job Creators Act, which would require the SEC's Office of the Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation to identify capital-access challenges facing rural small businesses.
